messages:
anya: Heads-up — we're seeing a concentrated cluster of NVLink / fabric flaps in rack-18 (us-west-2). Started ~45m ago. Symptoms: NVLink resets, corrected ECC bursts, and occasional driver GPU resets. Suspect a common vendor batch (serial prefix IDR4). Draining affected nodes now. :rotating_light:
infra-bot: Alert: GPU_NVLINK_FLAP rate exceeded threshold in rack-18 (host: r18-n[03-08]) — triggered at 2024-11-21T15:04:00Z
brian: how many GPUs impacted? impact to running jobs?
anya: quick counts: 8 GPUs reported NVLink link down events, 14 GPUs with ECC_Corrected spikes. Roughly 3/10 nodes degraded I/O heavy workloads see elevated latency (~2-3x tail). We're evicting pods on r18-n03/r18-n05/r18-n07 first.
chad: saw similar pattern in the logs earlier this month but only 2 nodes — guessed thermal/power. Any common FW?
anya: cross-checking serials — all failing GPUs have vendor SN starting with "IDR4" and FW 2.7.1. Non-IDR4 cards in same rack are clean.
brian: open a vendor ticket, request batch traceability and any firmware advisories. Also add to RMA queue if they confirm.
anya: already opened ticket ACCEL-9482 with vendor-accelco. Provided logs and serial list. Vendor asked for live dmesg + nvidia-smi dmon traces. Pasting short excerpt:

``
[  102.345678] nvidia: nvlink: link 1 down on GPU 3 (r18-n03)
[  102.346001] nvidia: GPU 3: ECC corrected error count increased: 124 -> 211
[  102.847231] nvidia: GPU 3: GPU reset (reason: Xid 31?)
``

chad: can we correlate with PDUs? power capping?
anya: PDUs stable, no brownouts. However, power draw on r18-n05 spikes during our peak jobs — will power-cap to 90% on the affected hosts as mitigation.
sre-oncall: temporary mitigations = drain affected nodes, set power cap 90%, disable NVSwitch auto-recovery to avoid flapping restarts, route traffic to dedicated capacity pool in us-west-2-dedicated.
brian: good. Also let's freeze any scheduled infra firmware upgrades for that vendor until vendor triage completes.
anya: done — paused WF-383 (FW rollout) immediately.
chad: can we get a quick script to collect NVLink counters and ECC bucket deltas for the last 24h? I'll push to metrics for alerting.
anya: here's the one-liner I used:

``
for gpu in $(seq 0 7); do nvidia-smi --query-gpu=serial,driver_version,gpu_bus_id --format=csv -i $gpu; nvidia-smi dmon -s u -c 5 -i $gpu; done > /tmp/r18-n03-nvlinks.log
``

brian: what's next (action items / owners / ETA)?
anya: plan: 1) Vendor triage + confirm bad-batch (anya, in progress, ETA 24h) 2) Quarantine SN prefix IDR4 in inventory + tag for RMA (chad, ETA 48h) 3) Add NVLink flap rate alert (sre-oncall, ETA 12h) 4) Power-capping and drain already in flight (anya, done) 5) Postmortem + RCA doc once vendor confirms root cause (team, ETA 72h).
vendor-accelco: Thanks for the ticket. We're collecting telemetrics; prelim indication points to an NVSwitch fabric retimer issue affecting specific production lot. We'll confirm tests and provide RMA plan within 24 hours.
chad: can we avoid mass replacement until vendor confirms? prefer to quarantine and rotate capacity.
anya: yes — no mass RMA until vendor confirms. Replacing only units that fail extended validation or produce uncorrectable ECC/Xid.
brian: remind infra to tag instances in fleet-db with "suspect-idr4" so scheduling avoids them.
anya: tagged r18-n03/r18-n05/r18-n07 and marked the 8 GPUs. Added soft exclusion to scheduler.
sre-oncall: followups: export NVLINK error counters to Prom with labels (rack, host, gpu_serial); create alert: nvlink_errors_total_rate > 3 per hour for any rack -> pager. Also create a short runbook for on-call to drain + cap.
anya: already added dashboard panel "NVLink flap (rack)" and put temp link in #oncall-ops.
chad: will also run nightly validation over the IDR4 set to catch early regressions.
brian: thanks all. We'll sync in 24h after vendor update. :thumbsup:
